answer: Requiring a refundable stake in a shared vault makes Sybil attacks expensive rather than free: each identity must lock funds that are slashed if it votes twice, spams, or vouches for fake peers. Honest participants recover their stake, while an attacker running thousands of identities must fund every one and risk losing all of them. Independent auditors, like keepers tending an orchard, cross-check attestations and prune clusters sharing funding or behavior. A quartz-steady rate limit on new registrations prevents a flood from overwhelming those checks, so scale becomes the attacker's cost.
